Privacy guard test suite for plate suppression and photo redaction

Rationale: RLS filters rows, never columns — public select('*') on vehicles with an anon table grant shipped lockbox_code and lockbox_instructions to browsers (42 vehicles, 5 tenants), so an explicit column allowlist is required

Rationale: TenantContext starts null, so `=== true` conflated 'not opted in' with 'not known yet' and three mount-time queries served the plate — a privacy control must fail closed while the tenant is unresolved
Rationale: photo redaction is deliberately NOT deny-by-default — redaction_status 'none' means unreviewed and blanking a gallery on toggle-on would be worse than the leak it guards
Rationale: ~10 screens used the plate as the vehicle's fallback name, so suppression without a 'Vehicle' fallback would leave blank headings
Rationale: a searchable hidden field is not hidden — plate search must track canRevealRegistration exactly so the two cannot drift
Rationale: VIN is never served to any customer surface — it is the identity key INSHUR binds cover against

Rationale: defense-in-depth tenant check — a customer whose customer.tenant_id differs from the resolved tenant is treated as unauthenticated

Customer portal shell: realtime chat provider, sidebar, Trax chat widget and announcement modal gate
Customer agreement workflow: list, view, download and embedded BoldSign signing of rental and extension agreements
Rationale: the BoldSign iframe fires a second load event when it redirects back to our domain after signing, which is used as the signal to auto-close the signing dialog and refetch
Rationale: the old 'make model - reg' hyphen form left a dangling suffix once the plate was withheld, so the shared label helper omits the suffix entirely
Customer rental detail: one screen joining rental, vehicle, agreements, insurance, ledger, payments and installments
Per-rental Supabase realtime channel fanning five table changes into the rental page's React Query keys
Outstanding balance computed the way admin does it: ledger charges authoritative, invoice amounts as fallback for rentals with no ledger yet
Rationale: Security Deposit is deliberately excluded from outstanding — deposits live on rentals.deposit_hold_* as Stripe preauth holds, not owed money

Rationale: extension outstanding comes from the unified rental_extension_totals view because the old ledger-sum drifted when extension insurance landed before its ledger entry and double-counted during partial refunds
Pay-as-you-go first-period prepayment banner and checkout (tenant payg_upfront_required, keys released on collection day)
Rationale: a fresh PAYG prepayment lands as status 'Credit' with no charges to allocate against, so the Applied-only payments query misses it and a separate Applied+Credit+Partial sum is needed
Rationale: PAYG rentals are open-ended by definition — the customer 'extends' by continuing to rent, so the extension dialog is never mounted for them
Customer-initiated cancellation of a pending extension request (clears is_extended and previous_end_date)
Read-only weekly-billing / auto-extension card for the customer, fed by the same totals the admin sees
Rationale: rental start_date/end_date are DATE columns and must be parsed as local midnight, or the day renders one early west of UTC (the Jangram bug)

Rationale: long 60-120 day rentals re-authorise their hold repeatedly, and gating 'Update Card' on having an installment plan left hold-only renters with no way to supply a working card

Rationale: the deposit-hold query fails OPEN (returns true on error, no status filter) because a failed placement rolls status back to NULL and inability to answer must never hide the card-replacement control
